name: static bool run_output_check(const output_check oc, const atf::fs::path& path, const std::string& stdxxx)
prose: Static function run_output_check(oc, path, stdxxx) in atf-sh/atf-check.cpp (lines 681-761) checks the captured output file path (stdxxx names the stream, "stdout" or "stderr", in the messages) against one output_check and returns true when the check passes. By oc.type: oc_empty passes when the file is empty and oc.negated is false, or non-empty and oc.negated is true; when it fails with negated false it prints "Fail: <stream> not empty" and a diff against /dev/null, and when it fails with negated true it prints only "Fail: <stream> is empty" (no diff and no file content); oc_file compares path with the file oc.value: a failure prints "does not match golden output" and a diff, or, when negated and equal, "matches golden output" and the golden file's content; oc_ignore always passes; oc_inline writes decode(oc.value) to a temporary file and compares it the same way (diff or the temporary file's content on failure); oc_match passes when some line of path matches the regular expression oc.value (grep_file, line by line) xor oc.negated, and on failure prints "Fail: regexp <re> not in/is in <stream>" followed by the whole file content; oc_save (which requires oc.negated to be false, checked with INV) copies path's bytes to the file named oc.value, truncating it, without checking for copy errors, and returns true; any other type reaches UNREACHABLE and returns false. Diagnostics go to stderr (the diff output is also connected to stderr). The helpers compare_files, grep_file and cat_file throw std::runtime_error when a file cannot be opened or read, in which case the function does not return normally.
note: Reviewers: original (oc_save requires !oc.negated, omitted; negated and match failures cat files rather than diffs) right (atf-check.cpp:704-707, 736-740, 744); round 15 (an oc_empty failure with negated true writes a diagnostic but no diff or file content) right (lines 692-694). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: bc_lex_token
prose: Function bc_lex_token(l) in bc/src/bc_lex.c (lines 170-504, compiled when BC_ENABLED); it must be called with the signal lock held (BC_SIG_ASSERT_LOCKED). It reads c = l->buf[l->i++], so l->i is incremented before the switch and the token describes the character that was at l->i on entry plus any further characters consumed. It sets l->t by character class: whitespace and NUL characters go to bc_lex_commonTokens; '!' gives BC_LEX_OP_REL_NE with '=' or BOOL_NOT otherwise (the latter with a POSIX diagnostic); '"' calls bc_lex_string; '#' gives a POSIX diagnostic and then bc_lex_lineComment (whitespace); '%', '*', '^', '/' (unless '/*', which starts a comment), '+', '-' pick the plain or assignment operator, '++' and '--' become increment and decrement; '&' and '|' require a doubled character for BC_LEX_OP_BOOL_AND/OR (with a POSIX diagnostic) and otherwise call bc_lex_invalidChar; '.' starts a number if a number character follows, otherwise it is BC_LEX_KW_LAST with a POSIX diagnostic; digits and the capital letters A to Z call bc_lex_number; lowercase letters call bc_lex_identifier (keyword or name); '(' ')' '[' ']' '{' '}' ',' ';' map to their punctuation tokens; '<' and '>' pick the relational, shift (only with BC_ENABLE_EXTRA_MATH) and assign variants; '=' gives '==' or assignment; backslash followed by a newline is whitespace and otherwise an invalid character; '$' and '@' are the truncate and places operators when BC_ENABLE_EXTRA_MATH is set; any other character calls bc_lex_invalidChar. Errors: bc_lex_invalidChar sets BC_LEX_INVALID and raises a parse error that does not return. The diagnostics for POSIX-forbidden constructs (the BC_ERR_POSIX_* codes) are errors only in the strict POSIX mode; otherwise, per bc_vm_handleError (vm.c:350-359), they print a warning when warnings are enabled and return silently when not, so the token is still produced and the function returns normally.
note: Reviewers: original (l->i is incremented before the switch, so the token corresponds to the character at l->i - 1 after the increment, i.e. at l->i on entry) right as a wording point, the old text already said 'on entry'; round 15 (POSIX-forbidden constructs are allowed in non-POSIX mode; no error is raised and the function returns normally) right (vm.c:350-359). Tally 2 right 0 wrong. I did not read bc_lex_commonTokens, bc_lex_number, bc_lex_identifier beyond their call conditions.

name: bc_parse_expr
prose: Function bc_parse_expr(p, flags) in bc/src/bc_parse.c (lines 2636-2640, compiled when BC_ENABLED); the packet slice 2038-2290 was inside bc_parse_expr_err, not this function. It asserts that p is non-NULL and calls bc_parse_expr_status(p, flags, bc_parse_next_read), returning nothing. bc_parse_expr_status calls bc_parse_expr_err(p, flags, next), which parses an expression allowed by flags and returns a status; when that status is BC_PARSE_STATUS_EMPTY_EXPR, bc_parse_expr_status itself raises BC_ERR_PARSE_EMPTY_EXPR with bc_parse_err; other errors are raised from inside bc_parse_expr_err (not read here). The parse results are stored in the parser and lexer state p.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the prose says reported parse errors come from bc_parse_expr_status, but the wrapper handles the returned status via bc_parse_err) wrong: the code that turns the empty-expression status into an error is in bc_parse_expr_status itself (bc_parse.c:2625-2633), which is what the old prose said; bc_parse_expr is only the thin caller (lines 2636-2640). Tally 0 right 1 wrong. bc_parse_expr_err (about 630 lines) was not read.

name: bc_history_enableRaw
prose: Static function bc_history_enableRaw(h) in bc/src/history.c (lines 821-877). On non-Windows builds it asserts BC_TTYIN, and if h->rawMode is already true it returns immediately without changing anything. Otherwise it takes the signal lock, saves the terminal attributes of stdin with tcgetattr into h->orig_termios (failure calls bc_vm_fatalError(BC_ERR_FATAL_IO_ERR), which does not return), releases the lock, copies the attributes, clears BRKINT, ICRNL, INPCK, ISTRIP and IXON from the input flags, sets CS8 in the control flags, clears ECHO, ICANON, IEXTEN and ISIG from the local flags, sets VMIN = 1 and VTIME = 0, and calls tcsetattr(STDIN_FILENO, TCSAFLUSH, &raw) with the lock held, repeating it while it fails with EINTR; a final failure calls bc_vm_fatalError(BC_ERR_FATAL_IO_ERR). On Windows nothing is done to the terminal here (the comment says raw mode is set in bc_history_init) and h->orig_termios is not touched. In every path that returns normally, h->rawMode is true afterwards.
note: Reviewers: original (on Windows rawMode is set without saving orig_termios) right (history.c:823-826, 876); round 15 (the precondition wrongly requires h->rawMode to be false, but the code returns early when it is true) right (history.c:832). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.
